title: When the Postcard Breaks
premise: Freya Reyes built her life on a forged name and twenty years of careful silence, running the only bookshop in Marrow Creek while raising her daughter alone. When a contested orchard deed names both her assumed identity and the man she once testified against—now released and searching for her—the past she buried arrives demanding answers. As she falls for Elias Thorne, the stubborn baker whose lease depends on the same parcel of land, Freya must decide whether to keep hiding or finally testify to what really happened that night. In the end, she chooses truth over safety, loses the bookshop but gains a family stitched from unlikely hands, and watches the orchard become something neither of them expected: home.
about_author: Kestrel Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who writes romances about people rebuilding themselves from wreckage. They live near an actual disputed orchard, which they insist is a coincidence.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A morning in Marrow Creek: opening the bookshop, school-run rituals with daughter Wren, the comfortable geometry of a life built to attract no attention. Beat: contentment shadowed by vigilance—we learn Freya checks the mail twice, always.

chapters.title: A Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The county clerk's letter arrives: the Hollis orchard deed lists both 'Freya Reyes' and 'Daniel Voss' as claimants through an old inheritance clause. Her hands go numb. Beat: the safe world cracks open on an ordinary Tuesday.

chapters.title: Bread and Boundaries
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Introduce Elias Thorne, whose bakery lease expires in ninety days unless he can buy the orchard parcel next door. He's blunt, warm, and annoyed at the bookshop owner who keeps dodging him. Beat: reluctant chemistry sparked by friction.

chapters.title: What Wren Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya digs out her old documents and we learn the truth in fragments: she witnessed a crime twenty years ago, entered protection, took a new name. Daniel Voss was her brother's employer—and her brother never came home. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man at the Counter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A stranger lingers in the bakery asking about 'a woman who used to be called something else.' Elias mentions the bookshop without thinking. Beat: guilt foreshadowed; the reader sees the danger Freya can't yet see.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Freya and Elias are forced into joint negotiations over the deed, trading sharp words over coffee and property lines. Beneath the sparring, mutual recognition of two tired survivors. Beat: enemies-to-allies pivot.

chapters.title: Found People
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The town rallies around the lease deadline—Wren's teacher, the retired sheriff, the knitting circle who meet in Freya's back room. Found-family theme surfaces: these people chose each other long before they knew why. Beat: warmth deepening stakes.

chapters.title: Voss Comes to Town
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Daniel Voss rents the room above the hardware store, polite and patient, buying bread every morning. Elias senses wrongness but can't name it. Beat: menace arriving dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: The Night I Ran
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, flashback chapter. Twenty years ago: the warehouse, the crime she saw, her brother Tomas's disappearance, the testimony that put Voss away and cost her everything. Beat: the full truth lands; sympathy becomes investment.

chapters.title: Postcards From Nowhere
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya finds a stack of unsigned postcards she mailed herself over the years—a ritual to prove she still existed. One is missing. Someone has been inside the shop. Beat: paranoia tightening; the title's meaning revealed.

chapters.title: Confession Over Flour
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Freya finally tells Elias everything at 2 a.m. in his kitchen. Instead of recoiling, he offers his bakery as a safehouse. Beat: love declared not in romance but in trust—the emotional midpoint.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Error
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Legal research reveals the deed's dual naming wasn't coincidence: someone petitioned to attach her old identity to the record, baiting her into the open. Voss didn't find her—he summoned her. Beat: reversal; hunter becomes architect.

chapters.title: Wren Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (first time). Twelve-year-old Wren has noticed the locked box, the fake birthday, the way her mother flinches at certain names. She confronts Freya gently. Beat: heartbreak and honesty; motherhood tested against secrecy.

chapters.title: Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The bakery lease expires; the landlord, pressured by an anonymous buyer, locks the doors. Elias loses everything except his recipes and his anger. Beat: rock bottom shared—both protagonists now have nothing left to protect but each other.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Old File
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Retired Sheriff Ada Brandt admits she always suspected Freya's file was buried improperly—that someone inside protected Voss's operation then, and maybe now. Beat: justice outside the law takes shape as a plan.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The group decides to use the deed meeting as a trap: get Voss to admit on record how he found Freya, exposing the corrupt clerk. Freya volunteers to be visible for the first time in twenty years. Beat: fear transmuted into agency.

chapters.title: The Orchard Meeting
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Under blossoming apple trees, Freya faces Voss. He is calm, almost tender, offering her a trade: walk away and he'll vanish. She refuses. Hidden recorder catches his confession about Tomas. Beat: climax begins; courage over survival instinct.

chapters.title: When It Breaks
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Voss realizes the trap; violence sparks in the orchard. Elias intervenes, Ada arrives with the recording already streaming to the state attorney, and Voss is taken—but not before revealing one last thing: Tomas may have survived. Beat: climax resolves, hope detonates.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya gives her real statement under her real name, reclaiming the identity she surrendered. The town stands witness in the courthouse gallery. Beat: catharsis; the price of survival finally paid forward into justice.

chapters.title: A Letter, Twenty Years Late
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A letter arrives postmarked from a town two states away, in handwriting she'd know anywhere. Tomas is alive, hiding for reasons of his own, and wants to come home. Beat: grief unclenches into trembling joy.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The town pools money—not charity, but shares—to reopen the bakery attached to the bookshop, one storefront with two doors. Elias asks Freya, plainly, to build something with him. Beat: romance fulfilled through partnership, not rescue.

chapters.title: The Postcard That Stays
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. One year later: Tomas at the counter, Wren shelving books, the orchard bearing fruit. Freya mails herself one last postcard—then keeps it, unsent, because she no longer needs proof she exists. Beat: peace earned; the arc closes on chosen belonging.
